sections.h2: What is Lamar County, Georgia known for?
sections.html:
Lamar County lies in west central Georgia between Atlanta and Macon, and Barnesville is the county seat. The state legislature created it in 1920 after Barnesville officials had asked four times, in 1869, 1906, 1912 and 1916. Land came from Monroe and Pike counties, leaving about 185 square miles of rolling country drained by streams that run to the Flint and Ocmulgee rivers.

Barnesville was once called the Buggy Capital of the South, and every September the town holds Buggy Days with a parade of original Barnesville buggies. Gordon State College, founded in 1872 and a four-year institution since 2007, is in town, and the Barnesville Expo Center combines a wetlands trail with a livestock arena. Pecan and peach groves cover the farmland, and the county's population climbed from 9,745 in the 1930 census to 18,500 in 2020.

sections.h2: How fast is Lamar County growing, and what does it mean for prices?
sections.html:
Lamar County has outgrown Johnson, Jones and Lanier counties since 2020, and the Census Bureau's estimates put the gain at 13.2% through July 2025.

A median value of $216,500 is the highest among the Johnson, Jones, Lamar and Lanier county figures. Permits for 136 homes in 2025 means new construction is competing with resale listings, and a 31.8-minute mean commute is the longest of the four counties. A seller with an older house should expect buyers to compare it against that new supply, and the assessors will value new and old homes as of the same January 1 date.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Lamar County property tax questions?
sections.html:
Lamar County runs tax work out of Barnesville, and the numbers below come from the county's own tax pages.

  • Tax Commissioner: 790 Veteran's Pkwy, Barnesville, GA 30204, mailing address P.O. Box 850, phone (770) 358-5162. The lobby is open Monday through Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., with a drive-thru window that closes a quarter hour earlier.
  • Tax Assessor: (770) 358-5161, for values and appeals.
  • Homestead filing: at the Tax Assessor's office, Monday to Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Clerk of Superior Court deed room: in the Lamar County Courthouse, for copies of a warranty deed.

The commissioner's website accepts online payment of property tax and car tag renewals. Lamar's county site says the commissioner does not set values or millage, so calling that office about a high valuation sends you to the wrong place.

sections.h2: When are Lamar County taxes due, and what happens after?
sections.html:
Lamar County bills are normally mailed by September 15 and due November 15, a schedule the county's FAQ says started with the 2018 tax year. That is earlier than the state's December 20 default, so owners used to other counties sometimes miss it.

  • After the due date, interest is charged at 1% per month on real estate and business personal property.
  • A 10% penalty applies to anything not paid within 90 days of the deadline.
  • If taxes stay unpaid more than 30 days past due, a fifa lien can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and credit bureaus may pick up the public record.
  • Mobile homes are due April 1, with a 10% filing penalty plus 1% per month, and an unpaid home can be sold at auction.

The Revenue Department adds that each taxpayer gets 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest begins, so check the postmark on yours. A written request for refund of tax that was erroneously or illegally collected must begin within three years of payment.

sections.h2: Which Lamar County homestead exemptions can I file for?
sections.html:
Applications are accepted from January 1 through April 1, and the Lamar County page says Georgia law allows no extension. Missing the window waives the exemption for that tax year. Once approved, it renews automatically until eligibility changes. Bring a driver license and either a 1040 or a signed income affidavit.

  • Regular state homestead (code S1), elderly at 62 (S3) and elderly at 65 (L4).
  • Disabled veteran (S5) and surviving spouse of a veteran (SS), with Veterans Administration proof of 100% service-connected disability.
  • Local county exemption for owners over 65: $20,000 off county maintenance and operation only.
  • Local school exemption for owners over 70: $7,000 off school maintenance and operation and school bonds.
  • Local disability exemption: $15,000 off school maintenance and operation, for total household income under $20,000, with a letter from two physicians or a Social Security letter declaring 100% disability.

The page says you must satisfy the state requirements before any local exemption applies. The state deferral program for homeowners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less is also available. For a mobile home to qualify for homestead, the owner of the home and the land beneath it must be the same person.

sections.h2: How does a Lamar County owner appeal a value?
sections.html:
The appraisal staff sets values from recent sales and market conditions as of January 1, and assessment notices usually go out in spring. You have 45 days from the notice date to appeal on grounds of taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption. File the written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors and name your chosen method. The county's Board of Equalization, appointed by the Grand Jury, hears the administrative appeals.

Georgia also offers preferential assessment for land. Lamar's page lists conservation use and residential transitional property under Georgia Code section 48-5-7.4, agricultural property under 48-5-7.4.1 and rehabilitated historic property under 48-5-7.2, each requiring a covenant of at least 10 years. Anyone selling acreage enrolled in one of these programs should ask the assessors what happens to the covenant when the deed changes hands.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Lamar County house with taxes still owed?
sections.html:
Ask the tax commissioner for a payoff that includes interest and penalty, then confirm with the Clerk of Superior Court whether a fifa has been recorded. A title company or closing attorney can send the payoff from the proceeds and release the lien. The Revenue Department states that whoever owns the property on January 1 owes the whole year's tax, which is why contracts commonly prorate it.

If the owner has died, ask the county Probate Court how to open the estate before anyone lists the house. A buyer purchasing for cash in Barnesville or the rural parts of the county will still want the tax payoff handled at closing.

faqs.q: When is the Lamar County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: November 15 for real estate and business personal property. Bills are normally mailed by September 15. Mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What penalty does Lamar County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest of 1% per month starts after the due date, and a 10% penalty applies to taxes unpaid within 90 days of the deadline. A fifa lien can be recorded after 30 days, per the county's FAQ.

faqs.q: Does Lamar County have extra exemptions for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners over 65 can claim a $20,000 county maintenance and operation exemption, and owners over 70 can claim $7,000 off school maintenance and operation and school bond tax. State requirements must be met first.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Lamar County?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $216,500 for owner-occupied housing in 2020-2024. The estimated population was 20,941 in July 2025.

faqs.q: Where do I file a homestead exemption in Lamar County?
faqs.a: At the Tax Assessor's office, between January 1 and April 1. Bring a driver license and a 1040 or a signed income affidavit.
